turns.content: Yaar meri shaadi mein six weeks bache hain. Rohan ko haldi mein hona hai, toast bhi dena hai — first year college se mera bhai hai. Par jab bhi Bangalore se travel ki baat karta hoon, bas "dekhte hain yaar, pakka try karunga." Main khud hi uski flight book kar doon kya, khatam jhanjhat?

Arre, stress mat le! 6 weeks ka time abhi kaafi hai, par main samajh sakta hoon kyun tension ho rahi hai. Shaadi ke time pe sab kuch sorted chahiye hota hai na?

Dekh, Rohan tera bhai jaisa hai, toh uska "dekhte hain" bolna shayad isliye hai kyunki woh apni work life ya travel plan ko lekar uncertain feel kar raha hoga. Bangalore se travel karna aur phir chutti lena thoda hectic ho sakta hai.

Meri advice? **Direct book mat kar abhi.** 

Ek baar usse thoda emotional hoke baat kar. Use bol, *"Bhai, tu nahi hoga toh haldi aur toast ka maza hi nahi aayega. Main chah raha hoon ki tujhe koi tension na ho, isliye pooch raha hoon—kya main tere liye tickets book kar doon ya tu khud kar lega?"*

Isse do cheezein hongi:
1. Use ehsaas hoga ki tu usse kitna miss karega (aur usse guilt bhi hoga agar woh nahi aaya).
2. Use clear ho jayega ki tu serious hai.

Agar woh phir bhi "dekhte hain" bole, toh bol de, *"Dekh, mujhe clarity chahiye taaki main arrangements kar sakun. Agar tu sure nahi hai, toh bata de, main kisi aur ko toast ke liye prepare kar loon."* Sometimes doston ko thoda 'push' chahiye hota hai taaki woh apne plans finalize karein.

Lekin haan, agar woh sach mein bahut busy hai aur tujhe pata hai ki woh aana chahta hai par manage nahi kar pa raha, toh tickets book kar dena ek bahut sweet gesture hoga. Par pehle baat kar le, warna bina bataye book karne se woh awkward bhi feel kar sakta hai.

Kya lagta hai, woh tujhse sach mein busy hone ki wajah se bol raha hai ya bas lazy ho raha hai?

Maine check kiya, nau hazaar ki return flight hai, koi bada amount nahi. Usne do mahine pehle job switch kiya, koi startup hai. Aur aajkal uske replies bhi two-word aate hain, pehle voice notes bhejta tha. Bol raha hoon khud ko ki busy hoga, par hafton se yahi chal raha hai.

Ye toh samajh mein aa raha hai ki tujhe sirf flight ki tension nahi hai, balki uske badle hue behavior ka bura lag raha hai. Aur ye bilkul valid hai—jab itna close friend ho, toh "two-word replies" aur voice notes ka band hona dil dukha deta hai.

Startup life ka pressure real hota hai, main maanta hoon. Nayi job, naye challenges, shayad woh wahan adjust karne mein hi poora exhausted ho raha ho. Par dosti mein itni chuppi thodi khatakti toh hai hi.

**Mera perspective ye hai:**

1.  **Ticket ka issue:** 9,000 rupaye tere liye badi baat nahi hai, lekin Rohan ke liye shayad ye "commitment" wali baat ban gayi hai. Agar tune ticket book kar di, toh uske upar ek obligation aa jayega aane ka. Agar woh nahi aaya, toh tujhe aur bura lagega.
2.  **Behavior ka issue:** Uske replies kam hone ka matlab ye bhi ho sakta hai ki woh stress mein hai aur use doston se baat karne ki energy nahi bach rahi. Kuch log jab overwhelm hote hain, toh woh "shutdown" ho jate hain.

**Meri suggestion:**
Ticket book karne se pehle, ek last *heart-to-heart* message bhej de. Kuch aisa:

*"Bhai, main dekh raha hoon tu kaafi busy hai aur humari baat bhi kam ho rahi hai. Sach bolun toh mujhe teri kami mehsoos ho rahi hai. Shaadi mein 6 hafte hain, aur main chahta hoon ki tu ho wahan. Agar startup ki wajah se tu stress mein hai, toh bata de, main samajh jaunga. Par please bas 'dekhte hain' bolke mujhe latka mat, mujhe clarity chahiye taaki main aage ka plan kar sakun."*

Ye message likhne se tu apne dil ka bojh halka kar dega.
*   Agar woh genuinely busy hai, toh woh samjhega ki tune use space di.
*   Agar woh bas ignore kar raha hai, toh tujhe clear ho jayega ki wahan se kya expect karna hai.

Agar iske baad bhi woh waisa hi behave kare, toh **ticket mat book karna.** Shaadi ke time pe toh tujhe woh log chahiye jo tere liye excited hon, jo tere saath khade hon. 

Tu bas ek baar clear baat kar le, taaki baad mein tujhe ye na lage ki tune try nahi kiya. Shaadi teri hai, focus apne happiness pe rakh, okay? 

Tu bata, agar woh nahi aaya toh kya tu handle kar lega emotional level pe?

Sach bolun toh ab bura lagne laga hai. Agar sach mein care karta toh pehle din haan bol deta na? Soch raha hoon aaj raat call karke seedha puchh loon — "bhai aa raha hai ya nahi, haan ya na." Kam se kam pata toh chalega main kahan khada hoon.

Bilkul sahi soch rahe ho. Kabhi-kabhi "haan ya na" sunna, us uncertainty mein jine se behtar hota hai. Jab dosti purani ho, toh ye "chup-chaap adjust karte rehna" dosti ko andar se khokhla kar deta hai.

Ek call karna perfect idea hai. Lekin, ek chhota sa tip doon?

Jab call karo, toh **confrontational tone mein mat karna.** Agar tum gusse mein poochoge "Aa raha hai ya nahi, haan ya na?", toh woh defensive ho jayega aur shaayad ladai ho jaye. Woh kahega, "Tu samajh kyun nahi raha, main kaam mein phasa hoon!" aur baat wahi khatam ho jayegi.

Iske bajaye, **vulnerability** ka use karo. Kuch aisa try karo:

*"Bhai, sun. Honestly, main thoda hurt hoon. Shaadi life ka bada event hai, aur mujhe lag raha hai ki main tujhe force kar raha hoon aane ke liye, jabki main chahta hoon ki tu khushi se aaye. Main tujhe call isliye kar raha hoon taaki mujhe clarity mile—kya tu aa raha hai? Kyunki agar tu nahi aa pa raha, toh main bura nahi maanunga, par mujhe bas abhi pata hona chahiye taaki main mental peace ke saath aage badh sakun."*

**Isse kya hoga?**
1.  Tumne apni feelings share kar di (hurt ho).
2.  Tumne use "out" de diya (agar woh nahi aa sakta, toh tum respect karoge).
3.  Tumne use force nahi kiya, bas apni zarurat batayi.

Agar woh iske baad bhi vague reh raha hai ya bol raha hai "dekhte hain," toh samajh lena ki uski priority abhi kuch aur hai. Phir tumhe pata chal jayega ki tum kahan khade ho—aur tum uske bina bhi apni shaadi enjoy karne ke liye mentally ready ho jaoge.

Call kar lo aaj raat. Dil halka ho jayega. Aur jo bhi result nikle, yaad rakhna—shaadi tumhari khushi ka din hai, kisi ek insaan ka "na" aana tumhare celebration ko kharab nahi kar sakta.

Sab badhiya hoga. Call ke baad batana kya hua, okay? I'm rooting for you.

Meri fiancée bol rahi hai main overthink kar raha hoon, woh bas busy hoga. Par yeh wahi banda hai jo 2019 mein meri behen ki shaadi ke liye overnight bus se aaya tha. Kuch toh badla hai aur samajh nahi aa raha kya, aur haldi se do hafte pehle main usse naraaz baitha hoon, yeh feeling hi ganda hai.

I hear you, and that hurts. It’s not "overthinking" when you have a benchmark like 2019. If someone went through the trouble of an overnight bus for your sister’s wedding, then yes, they *know* how to show up when it matters.

When you compare that version of him to the current "two-word replies" version, it’s natural to feel like something is broken. Your fiancée is trying to be rational—maybe she’s looking at it from the outside—but she doesn’t have the history with him that you do.

Here is the thing about friendships: **Sometimes, people change, and sometimes, they just get lost in their own mess.**

Maybe he *is* just overwhelmed by his new startup. Maybe he’s struggling with money and is too embarrassed to say it. Maybe he’s depressed and isolating himself. Or maybe, unfortunately, you two are just drifting apart. 

**But here is why you need to make that call tonight:**

You don't want to carry this "naraazgi" (resentment) into your Haldi. Imagine standing there, glowing, happy, and having a tiny voice in the back of your head saying, *"Where is he? Why isn't he here? Did I ask him enough? Is he ignoring me?"* That will ruin your mood more than his absence ever could.

**Do this for yourself, not for him:**

1.  **The Call:** Don't make it about "holding him accountable." Make it about **"clearing the air."**
2.  **The Approach:** Bring up the 2019 memory. It’s a powerful tool. Say: *"Bhai, remember 2019? You came all the way for my sister’s wedding. That meant the world to me. And honestly, that’s why I’m feeling so weird right now. I feel like we’re drifting, and this whole 'shaadi' thing feels like a wall between us. Are we okay? Is everything fine in your life?"*

If he’s a real friend, that will break his shell. He might just say, *"Yaar, I'm so sorry, I've been drowning in work/stress and I didn't realize I was being a jerk."* 

If he stays cold, then you have your answer. And the best part? **You will have closure.**

You’ll know you did everything a brother would do. If he chooses not to show up after that, then let him go. Don’t let his current state of mind steal your joy. Your Haldi is about *you*, your love, and the people who *are* there, not the one who isn't.

Does that feel like a better way to frame it? Taking the power back into your own hands?
